sourcedFrom: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) (not printed on the document)
cleanIntro: The Vanguard Series 2 is a push-feed bolt rifle with a hinged floorplate magazine, and Weatherby's own instruction is that it must be disassembled before it can be properly cleaned — bolt out, trigger guard and stock off the barrelled action. Two things on this rifle decide how the job goes. The bolt is released by a BOLT RELEASE LEVER on the receiver, not by pulling the trigger — that is the Mark V's method and the two books otherwise read almost identically, so the distinction is worth holding on to. And the trigger assembly is cleaned with compressed air and NOTHING else: no solvent, no oil, ever. Reassembly torque is a real specification here and it branches on what your stock is made of, so read that step rather than guessing. ⚠ On early Vanguard Series 2 rifles the intermediate SAFE position is marked with a "U" — check your own rifle's markings before trusting the safety positions described below.

steps.title: Safety to OFF SAFE, then open the bolt
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, fingers out of the trigger guard. Move the manual safety lever to OFF SAFE — on this rifle the bolt cannot be lifted with the safety fully engaged. Then lift the bolt handle until it stops and pull the bolt rearward against the bolt stop; the chambered cartridge is extracted and thrown clear of the receiver.
steps.prose: ⚠ On early Vanguard Series 2 rifles the intermediate SAFE position was marked with a "U" rather than the current marking, so read your own bolt sleeve before you trust the detents.
steps.quote: 2. To remove a cartridge from the chamber, open the bolt by lifting the bolt handle until it stops and pulling the bolt to the rear until the bolt stops against the bolt stop. The cartridge will be ejected from the receiver.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Unloading the Rifle — p.9

steps.title: Confirm the chamber actually gave the round up
steps.action: Check the chamber both by eye and by feel. If a live round or a fired case is still sitting in there after the bolt has come back, stop: Weatherby's instruction is to remove the bolt and take the rifle to a service centre or gunsmith with the bolt kept OUT of the rifle. Do not try to lever, tap or drive a stuck case out yourself.
steps.quote: 3. Visually and manually check to make certain that the bolt has extracted any live round or fired cartridge case from the chamber. If a live round or fired cartridge case remains in the chamber, remove the bolt, (refer to Removing The Bolt Assembly From The Receiver, page 7) and immediately take the rifle to a Weatherby service center or a qualified gunsmith, keeping the bolt out of the rifle at all times.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Unloading the Rifle — p.9

steps.title: Drop the floorplate and empty the magazine into your hand
steps.action: Press the floorplate release and the floorplate swings open, letting the magazine column drop out. Catch the cartridges — do not let them hit the ground. A dented or dirtied rifle cartridge is not a cosmetic problem: Weatherby's own warning is that loading a damaged or dirty round can jam a live cartridge in the chamber.
steps.quote: 4. To unload the magazine, open the floorplate by depressing the floorplate release (refer to Fig. 6). The floorplate will swing out, allowing the cartridges to drop free. Do not allow the cartridges to fall to the ground as they may be damaged or become dirty, making loading and chambering more difficult. Subsequent loading of a damaged or dirty cartridge may cause a live round to become jammed in the chamber of the firearm, resulting in an unsafe condition.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Unloading the Rifle — p.9

steps.title: Reconfirm empty, reseat the follower, close the floorplate
steps.action: Look and feel again — magazine box and chamber both. Then push the magazine follower back down inside the magazine box and swing the floorplate shut so it latches. A follower left cocked up in the box will not let the floorplate close square, and it will foul the stock when the action comes out.
steps.quote: 5. Visually and manually reconfirm that there are no cartridges remaining in the magazine or chamber. 6. Reposition the magazine follower inside the magazine box and close the floorplate.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Unloading the Rifle — p.9

steps.title: Safety to middle SAFE, bolt back, and LOOK once more
steps.action: Set the safety lever to the middle SAFE position, raise the bolt handle and draw the bolt all the way rearward. Now look into the chamber and the magazine one final time before anything is unscrewed. Weatherby prints this instruction in capitals at the head of the disassembly, which is the tell that it is not a formality.
steps.quote: 1. Move the safety lever to the middle “SAFE” position (refer to Manual Safety Operation, page 5). 2. Unload the rifle (refer to Unloading the Rifle, page 9). 3. Raise the bolt handle and draw the bolt all the way to the rear. 4. VISUALLY CHECK THE CHAMBER AND THE MAGAZINE TO BE CERTAIN THERE ARE NO CARTRIDGES IN THE RIFLE.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Disassembly of the Vanguard Rifle — p.10

steps.title: Bolt release lever pressed, bolt straight out the back
steps.action: Move the safety to OFF SAFE, run the bolt back until it stops against the bolt stop, then press the BOLT RELEASE LEVER as far as it will go and draw the bolt straight rearward out of the receiver. The lever is the whole mechanism on a Vanguard — you do not pull the trigger to release the bolt, and doing so achieves nothing here.
steps.prose: This is the single biggest difference between this rifle and the Mark V in the next Weatherby book, whose bolt IS released by pulling the trigger. Do not carry that method over.
steps.quote: 5. Depress the bolt release lever as far as possible (refer to Fig. 5). 6. Move the bolt straight rearward until the bolt clears the receiver
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Removing the Bolt Assembly from Receiver — p.7

steps.title: Floorplate open, both trigger guard screws out, stock off
steps.action: Press the floorplate release to open the floorplate — the front trigger guard screw hides behind it. With a properly fitting screwdriver, remove the front and rear trigger guard screws, lift the trigger guard assembly out of the stock and separate the stock from the barrelled action. Keep the two screws apart: they are DIFFERENT LENGTHS and the short one is the front.
steps.caution: Failure to strictly adhere to the disassembly and assembly instructions contained herein
steps.quote: a. Press the floorplate release to open the floorplate (refer to Fig. 6). b. With a screwdriver of the proper size, remove the front and rear trigger guard screws. c. Remove the trigger guard assembly from the stock. d. Remove the stock from the barreled action.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Disassembly of the Vanguard Rifle — p.10

steps.title: Bolt sleeve rotated clockwise ~170°, firing pin assembly out
steps.action: Hold the bolt body still in one hand and rotate the bolt sleeve CLOCKWISE as seen from the rear, roughly 170 degrees, until the firing pin and bolt sleeve assembly breaks free of the bolt body. Then withdraw that assembly straight out of the bolt body. It is under mainspring load, so keep a hand on it as it separates rather than letting it spring apart.
steps.quote: 1. Refer to Fig. 7 (below) and hold the bolt body (B) stationary while rotating the bolt sleeve (A) in a clockwise direction (as viewed from the rear) approximately 170° until the firing pin/bolt sleeve assembly separates from the bolt body (B). 2. Withdraw the firing pin/bolt sleeve assembly (A) from the bolt body (B) (refer to Fig. 7).
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Disassembly of the Bolt Assembly — p.10

steps.title: Field strip complete — and this is Weatherby's limit
steps.action: The Vanguard is now in its published pieces: barrelled action, stock, trigger guard assembly with its two screws, bolt body, and the firing pin/bolt sleeve assembly. Weatherby stops here for the Vanguard and says so plainly — further disassembly is not recommended and could damage the rifle, and anything beyond this goes to a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or a qualified gunsmith. Do not attempt to strip the firing pin assembly or the trigger.
steps.quote: Further disassembly is not recommended and could result in damage to your rifle. If further disassembly is required, please contact a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Disassembly of the Bolt Assembly — p.10

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, brush centred at the muzzle
steps.action: With the bolt out, run a correctly sized bore brush wet with solvent from the CHAMBER end right out of the muzzle, then draw it carefully back through — keeping the brush centred in the muzzle as it comes out is what protects the crown, and a damaged crown costs accuracy permanently. Follow with patches on a jag, chamber end first, until they emerge clean.
steps.quote: 3. Starting from the chamber end, push the cleaning rod all the way through the bore, allowing it to exit the muzzle, then carefully draw it back through the bore, ensuring that the brush stays centered in the muzzle as it is withdrawn. Repeat several times.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Cleaning the Bore — p.12

steps.title: Oil the bore, then take the oil back out
steps.action: Push one lubricant-saturated patch through from the chamber end, then a dry clean patch behind it to take the excess straight back out. That second patch is not optional housekeeping — oil standing in the bore or chamber can raise chamber pressure or act as a partial obstruction. Finish with a light film of lubricant wiped around the muzzle.
steps.quote: 7. Insert a patch saturated with gun lubricant into the cleaning rod tip and push it through the bore from the chamber end. Remove the patch and withdraw the rod. 8. Insert a dry, clean patch into the cleaning rod tip and push it through the bore starting at the chamber end to remove excess lubricant. Remove the patch and withdraw the rod.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Cleaning the Bore — p.12
steps.warn: Excess lubrication in the bore or chamber of any firearm may create excessive chamber pressures or a partial bore obstruction, resulting in possible damage to the firearm and serious injury to the shooter and bystanders upon firing. BE SURE ALL EXCESS LUBRICANT HAS BEEN REMOVED.

steps.title: Receiver inside and out, then the bolt parts
steps.action: Clean the inside and outside of the receiver with solvent on a lint-free cloth, using a plastic-bristle brush to get into the recesses and the lug raceways, then dry it. Do the bolt parts the same way, with a small brush into the bolt sleeve recesses and around the firing pin spring. Light oil on both, and wipe the surplus off.
steps.aside: 1. Clean all parts with a gun cleaning solvent and dry with a clean cloth. Use of a small brush will help in cleaning the recesses of the bolt sleeve and the firing pin spring.
steps.quote: 1. Using a small lint-free cloth, clean the inside and outside of the receiver with gun-cleaning solvent and dry thoroughly with a clean cloth. Use of a plastic bristle gun cleaning brush will help to clean the recesses of the receiver.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Cleaning the Receiver — p.13

steps.title: Trigger assembly: compressed air ONLY, no oil
steps.action: Blow the trigger's internals out with compressed air and leave it at that. Weatherby is explicit that no lubrication is required inside the trigger assembly, and if oil has crept into the housing the answer is more air and a wipe, not more oil. Wear eye protection while you do it.
steps.prose: Oil in a rifle trigger collects grit and then freezes in cold weather; a Vanguard trigger that has been 'lubricated' is a trigger waiting to fail in the field.
steps.quote: Using compressed air, blow the internal components of the trigger assembly off to remove any loose dirt and debris. No lubrication is required on the internal components of the trigger assembly. If oil seeps into the trigger housing, blow out the internals with compressed air again and wipe off any excess oil residue.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Cleaning the Trigger Assembly — p.14
steps.warn: Always wear eye protection when using compressed air to avoid injury to eyes by foreign objects.

steps.title: Magazine, trigger guard and stock
steps.action: Wipe the inside of the magazine box, the follower and its spring with solvent, dry them, then oil lightly and remove the excess. Brush the exposed surfaces of the trigger guard assembly with solvent and dry it. The stock usually needs no more than a clean dry or silicone cloth — but if the rifle has been out in the wet, let it dry fully before it goes back together.
steps.caution: If you have been hunting or shooting in wet weather, special cleaning may be required (refer to Rust Prevention and Repair, below) and allow the stock to dry thoroughly before reassembly and storage.
steps.quote: NOTE: Do not use acetone or any abrasive solvent cleaners on carbon fiber stocks. This can jeopardize the external coating of the carbon fiber.
steps.cite: VANGUARD® — Owner's Manual — Feb 18 2022 (date carried in the published filename; no printed edition code) — Cleaning the Stock — p.14

deepAbsentReason: Weatherby publishes nothing beyond the strip above for the Vanguard Series 2. Its own words at the end of the bolt disassembly are that further disassembly is not recommended and could result in damage to the rifle, and that anything further goes to a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or a qualified gunsmith. The book's trigger section forbids any adjustment other than the single pull-weight screw and any modification at all. There is therefore no deeper published procedure to walk, and inventing one would be inventing a deep clean.

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Bolt out first — always clean from the CHAMBER end.
Solvent-wet bore brush through and back, brush kept centred in the muzzle to protect the crown.
Patches on a jag from the chamber end until they emerge clean.
All solvent removed from the muzzle, then one lubricant patch, then a dry patch to take the excess out.
Light film of lubricant wiped around the muzzle itself.

cleaning.name: Barrel exterior and receiver
tasks: Solvent-wet cloth over all accessible barrel and receiver surfaces; brush into the corners and recesses.
All solvent removed with a dry lint-free cloth.
Light coat of lubricant, excess wiped off.
Removable muzzle brake, if fitted: unscrew counter-clockwise viewed from the muzzle, brush the bore of the brake and its threads clean.

cleaning.name: Bolt assembly
tasks: All parts cleaned in solvent and dried.
Small brush into the bolt sleeve recesses and around the firing pin spring.
Light coat of gun oil on all accessible surfaces, excess removed.

cleaning.name: Magazine and trigger guard
tasks: Inside of the magazine, the follower and the spring cleaned with solvent and dried.
Light lubricant inside the magazine and on follower and spring, excess removed.
Trigger guard assembly brushed with solvent and dried.

cleaning.name: Trigger assembly
tasks: Compressed air ONLY — blow out loose dirt and debris.
NO lubrication inside the trigger assembly, ever.
If oil has seeped in, blow it out again and wipe the residue off.
Eye protection while using compressed air.

cleaning.name: Stock and rust prevention
tasks: Clean dry cloth or silicone cloth is normally enough.
No acetone or abrasive solvent cleaners on carbon fibre stocks.
After a wet outing: allow 2-3 hours at room temperature for metal to dry completely, then a liberal coat of high-grade gun oil, excess wiped off.
Surface rust: plastic-bristle brush and solvent; if it will not come off, a service centre or gunsmith — do not leave it.

reassembly: Firing pin/bolt sleeve assembly into the bolt body, aligning the square boss on the bolt sleeve shank with the indexing groove on the bolt body.
Rotate the firing pin/bolt sleeve assembly counter-clockwise (viewed from the rear) until the nose of the cocking piece drops into the detent near the cam opening.
Empty magazine box into its cavity on the underside of the stock, pushed fully in so it mates with the receiver.
Rifle held vertical: trigger guard assembly, with follower and follower spring, into its cavity and held there.
Rifle turned horizontal, trigger guard up; SHORT screw to the front, LONG screw to the rear.
A small amount of blue (non-permanent) thread locking compound on both trigger guard screws.
Both screws lightly tightened, then the barrel pulled rearward to seat barrel and receiver properly in the stock.
Front screw torqued to 35 inch pounds, then the rear to 35 inch pounds — that is FINAL for wood and synthetic stocks; over-torquing damages the stock.
Composite stocks with aluminium bedding blocks or pillars ONLY: a further 55 inch pounds front, then 55 inch pounds rear.

Bolt back into the receiver: safety to middle SAFE, nose of the bolt into the rear of the receiver, bolt release lever depressed, bolt forward about three inches, release the lever, then close the bolt.
fncheck: With the rifle proven empty and the muzzle safe: work the bolt through several full cycles and confirm it lifts, runs and locks with no binding and that the bolt release holds it in. Check the safety lever in all three positions and confirm it moves positively — on an early Series 2 the middle SAFE position may be marked "U". Open and close the floorplate and confirm it latches shut. Confirm the bore is clear of patches and free of standing oil before loading. If the trigger guard screws were disturbed, re-check both torques against the value for YOUR stock material.
